tools.name: ListTicketComments
tools.description:
Get all comments for a specific Zendesk ticket, including the original description.

The first comment is always the ticket's original description/content.
Subsequent comments show the conversation history.

Each comment includes:
- author_id: ID of the comment author
- body: The comment text
- created_at: Timestamp when comment was created
- public: Whether the comment is public or internal
- attachments: List of file attachments (if any) with file_name, content_url, size, etc.

parameters.name: ticket_id
parameters.description: The ID of the ticket to get comments for

output.description: A dictionary containing the ticket comments, metadata, and ticket URL

tools.name: ListTickets
tools.description:
List tickets from your Zendesk account with offset-based pagination.

By default, returns tickets sorted by ID with newest tickets first (desc).

Each ticket in the response includes an 'html_url' field with the direct link
to view the ticket in Zendesk.

PAGINATION:
- The response includes 'next_offset' when more results are available
- To fetch the next batch, simply pass the 'next_offset' value as the 'offset' parameter
- If 'next_offset' is not present, you've reached the end of available results

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only include tickets with this status. Defaults to 'open'

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of tickets to return. Defaults to 30

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of tickets to skip before returning results. Defaults to 0

parameters.name: sort_order
parameters.description: Sort order for tickets by ID. 'asc' returns oldest first, 'desc' returns newest first. Defaults to 'desc'

output.description: A dictionary containing tickets list (each with html_url), count, and pagination metadata. Includes 'next_offset' when more results are available

tools.name: SearchArticles
tools.description:
Search for Help Center articles in your Zendesk knowledge base.

This tool searches specifically for published knowledge base articles that provide
solutions and guidance to users. At least one search parameter (query or label_names)
must be provided.

PAGINATION:
- The response includes 'next_offset' when more results are available
- To fetch the next batch, simply pass the 'next_offset' value as the 'offset' parameter
- If 'next_offset' is not present, you've reached the end of available results
- The tool automatically handles fetching from the correct page based on your offset

IMPORTANT: ALL FILTERS CAN BE COMBINED IN A SINGLE CALL
You can combine multiple filters (query, labels, dates) in one search request.
Do NOT make separate tool calls - combine all relevant filters together.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Search text to match against articles. Supports quoted expressions for exact matching. Defaults to no text search.

parameters.name: label_names
parameters.description: Only include articles that have at least one of these label names (case-insensitive). Available on Professional/Enterprise plans only. Defaults to any labels.

parameters.name: created_after
parameters.description: Only include articles created after this date (format: YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to no lower date bound.

parameters.name: created_before
parameters.description: Only include articles created before this date (format: YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to no upper date bound.

parameters.name: created_at
parameters.description: Only include articles created on this exact date (format: YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to any creation date.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: Field to sort articles by. Defaults to relevance according to the search query

parameters.name: sort_order
parameters.description: Sort order direction. Defaults to descending

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of articles to return. Defaults to 30

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of articles to skip before returning results. Defaults to 0

parameters.name: include_body
parameters.description: Include article body content in results. Bodies will be cleaned of HTML and truncated. Defaults to True

parameters.name: max_article_length
parameters.description: Maximum length for article body content in characters. 0 returns the whole body. Defaults to 500

output.description: Article search results with pagination metadata. Includes 'next_offset' when more results are available. Simply use this value as the 'offset' parameter in your next call to fetch the next batch

summary:
The Zendesk toolkit connects Arcade to your Zendesk account, enabling agents and apps to manage support tickets, read conversations, resolve issues, and search Help Center articles programmatically.

## Capabilities

- **Ticket management**: Create comments on existing tickets, mark tickets as solved (with an optional closing comment), and retrieve direct `html_url` links to any ticket in the Zendesk UI.
- **Ticket listing & pagination**: List tickets sorted by newest-first with offset-based pagination — pass `next_offset` from each response to walk through result pages.
- **Conversation history**: Fetch all comments on a ticket in chronological order, including the original description, author IDs, public/internal status, timestamps, and file attachments.
- **Knowledge base search**: Search published Help Center articles by free-text query and/or label names, with combined-filter support and offset pagination.
- **Identity & account context**: Retrieve the authenticated user's profile, role, organization, and Zendesk account details.

## OAuth

This toolkit uses OAuth 2.0. The auth provider is **Zendesk**. See the [Arcade Zendesk auth provider docs](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/references/auth-providers/zendesk) for setup instructions.

## Secrets

- **`ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN`** — Your Zendesk subdomain, i.e., the `<subdomain>` part of `https://<subdomain>.zendesk.com`. This is not a generated credential; it is simply the unique subdomain assigned to your Zendesk account when it was created. You can find it by logging into Zendesk and inspecting the URL in your browser. No special permissions or account tier are required to obtain it.

Configure secrets in the [Arcade secrets dashboard](https://api.arcade.dev/dashboard/auth/secrets) and refer to the [Arcade secrets guide](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/guides/create-tools/tool-basics/create-tool-secrets) for integration details.
